main_text.p: modi hominem scripsit, caput illud, quod ex suo opere expunctum fuisse conquestus fuerat, repraesentavit. In hoc autem capite Morinum mire suggil-lat, qui mera criminandi intemperantia{m} & carpendi libidine multa Evangelicis objecerit, Facile est inquit Capellus, ({m}Ignaræ plebi fumos vendere, & ad populum phaleras jactare atque ostentare ; at nunquam doctis, ne mediocriter quidem Hebraicè peritis, persuadere poterit Morinus, non potuisse viros, qui post Hieronymum surrexerunt, longe doctissimos quam plurima in ejus translatione observare gravissima σφάλματα atque hallucinationes.

Multum tamen tribuit idem Capellus veteribus translationibus, ob ea-rum antiquitatem & perpetuum Ecclesiae usum; sed ferre non potest, ut iis locis, ubi manifesto vitiosæ sunt, præponatur earum vitium authentico textui, aut a-liis translationibus longè acceuratiori-bus: quare Morinum arguit, ut planè iniquum, qui autoritatem septuaginta Inter-

page.notes: The printed text ends in a line of the fragment "Inter-" as a catchword. Uncertain readings: "acceuratiori-" is printed with a doubled-looking "cc" and "ce" and may be a printing error for "accuratiori-"; left as printed. The italic/roman boundaries in "Hebraicè peritis, persuadere poterit Morinus" are hard to determine from the scan and may be off. The superscript reference mark after "intemperantia" is a printed asterisk-like sign; I have marked it {m}, but it may be a different sign, and the reference to "(m)" in the text is set in italic parentheses. Long s has been normalised to s throughout.
